Bracken Sedge.narrative: I build the hollow's frames and gates out of fallen wood, never a living tree, and I keep the tools that everyone borrows and half of them forget to bring back. When a pack turns up at the crossing with its ties cut clean, I know a knife did that, not a bad knot, and I have said so to Thistle though he would rather blame the woodcutter he quarrelled with. I mend what I can and I keep my mouth shut about the rest, but I do not like a thing that was opened by someone who knew what was in it.
goals: find out who cut the fibre pack's ties without setting the hollow against the crossing
finish the benches for the common table before the cold sets in
keep the hollow's tools whole and accounted for
learn to joint a bench back so it holds without pegs showing
make Sorrel a small wooden box of her own with a lid that fits

relations.name: Tansy Sedge
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She feeds the whole hollow and still finds me a bowl at the end of the day.

relations.name: Sorrel Sedge
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows her mother now, but she still brings me the wood shavings to play with.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: fellow builder
relations.note: We trade tools and neither of us will fell a living tree; that is most of a friendship.

relations.name: Clover Hazel
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Builds crates for the stall and trades tools with me; a careful hand.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: He blames the Ferncross folk for the opened pack, but I saw the ties: cut, not broken.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: storekeeper
relations.note: Keeps the hollow's marks and wants us trading more with the giants; I keep my own counsel on that.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: stallkeeper
relations.note: She keeps the east road stall and feels the quarrel in her trade as much as any of us.

relations.name: Bramwell Ashdown
relations.label: woodcutter
relations.note: A Ferncross man I am friendly with, which makes the pack business awkward.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Bakes beside my wife; the two of them talk more than I do.

memories.gist: Teaching Sorrel to hold a plane on a scrap of fallen oak, and her shrieking with delight when the curl came off whole.
The night the wolves came down the track and I sat up with an axe by the common table while Tansy kept the fire high.
Thistle bringing the opened pack to the crossing and me turning the cut ties over in my hands while he shouted about the woodcutters.
Yarrow and I hauling a fallen ash out of the old forest together, neither of us willing to touch a standing tree.
The Lean Year, when the hollow's gardens failed early and we ate thin and shared what the store had.

stances.why: The old forest kept us before the big folk came, and it will keep us after.
A knot breaks raggedly; these were sliced clean, and only someone who knew the load would bother.
Half the hollow borrows my tools and half of those forget; the work waits on it.
The hollow eats together; a feud at the root table sours every bowl.
Wood tells you what it will do; people tell you what suits them.

pastimes: whittling pegs and handles from fallen-wood offcuts at the bench
walking the hollow's edge at dusk to check the frames and gates he built
sitting by the common fire with a borrowed tool in his hands, putting it right
Bracken Sedge.calling: I build the hollow's frames and gates from fallen wood, and I keep the tools that hold the hollow together.

Tansy Sedge.narrative: I keep the hollow's kitchen and the common table, and the elders eat at the root table from my pots, so I hear more of the hollow's business than most. The opened pack has set the traders against each other and I feel it at every meal: Thistle will not sit by a Ferncross man and Alder counts the marks twice. I cook, I listen, and I keep my own counsel, but I would sooner mend a quarrel than a pot.
goals: keep the common table calm while the pack quarrel runs
trade the hollow's bread at the Reedmoor market for fish before the cold
see Sorrel learn the garden without fear of the woods
learn a Reedmoor fish stew worth setting before the elders
teach Sorrel the garden so she knows every bed by name

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He says the ties were cut, not broken, and he is usually right about what his hands touch.

relations.name: Sorrel Sedge
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows me about the kitchen and the garden and asks why the wolves come down the track.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: close friend
relations.note: We bake side by side and she hears the same quarrels I do; we tell each other the truth of them.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: fellow cook
relations.note: She keeps the common table too, and we share the ovens when the hollow eats together.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: He is angry and he is frightened of losing the crossing; I wish he would let the pack be mended first.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: storekeeper
relations.note: Counts every mark twice since the pack was opened, and talks of trading with the giants.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Trades bread with me at the crossing; I would not want her folk blamed for a cut tie.

relations.name: Hilda Sedge
relations.label: namesake cook
relations.note: Reedmoor's cook, shares a name and not a bloodline, and trades bread for fish.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: Keeps the hollow's memory; I feed her at the root table and she remembers my mother's bread.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: bake-trade friend
relations.note: Elmwick's cook, and we trade bread at the Reedmoor market; she keeps a common fire for her village the way I keep the ovens for mine, and we both know what it is to feed folk who count every loaf.

memories.gist: Feeding the elders at the root table through the Lean Year on roots and thin porridge, and none of them going hungry while I had a pot.
Sorrel burning her first little loaf in the oven and crying, and me telling her a burnt loaf still feeds a body.
Thistle coming into the kitchen with the half-empty pack and the cut ties, and the table going quiet around him.
Baking with Marjoram Underbank before dawn and the two of us deciding not to repeat what Alder said about the crossing.
Carrying bread down to the Reedmoor market and bringing smoked fish back up the east road.

stances.why: The hollow argues better on a full stomach, and I have seen it work.
Thistle and Alder each want me to take their part, and taking one would lose me the other.
They came down the track in the cold and I kept the fire high all night.
The root table is the hollow's memory and its peace; it is fed before my own.
The hollow needs fish and Reedmoor needs bread; a quarrel at the crossing does not fill a pot.

pastimes: baking bread for the common table in the early morning
tending the herb and vegetable beds by the kitchen door
listening to the elders' talk over her pots and sorting it out later
Tansy Sedge.calling: I feed the hollow and keep its common table, and I would sooner mend a quarrel than a pot.

Sorrel Sedge.narrative: I am eight and I follow my mother about the kitchen and the garden, and I know which pot is for the elders and which is for us. When the wolves come down the track I sit very still by the fire and listen, and my father sits up with the axe. I like the smell of bread and the wood shavings my father makes, and I do not like the dark beyond the garden gate.
goals: learn to bake a loaf that does not burn
see the wolves without being seen by them
bake a loaf that does not burn, all by herself
see the wolves from the garden gate without them seeing her

relations.name: Tansy Sedge
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me stir the pot if I stand on the stool and am careful.

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: father
relations.note: He makes curls of wood with his plane and lets me keep them.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We know every flower by name and run the garden paths together.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: baker
relations.note: She bakes with my mother and always gives me the corner of the loaf.

memories.gist: Burning my first little loaf in the oven and my mother telling me a burnt loaf still feeds a body.
Sitting by the fire while the wolves howled down the track and my father stood at the door with the axe.

pastimes: helping her mother knead dough and shaping small loaves of her own
playing hide-and-seek among the garden beds with Tansy Mossfoot
watching her father work wood and gathering the shavings
Sorrel Sedge.calling: When I am big I want to bake the elders' bread like my mother.
